data.standardized_narrative: In 2020, Syndicate 623 reported a net release of prior year reserves totaling $16.5 million, representing a 2.0% release of opening gross claims outstanding. This favourable development was primarily driven by releases in the property and reinsurance divisions, benefiting from benign claims experience related to 2019 natural catastrophe events such as Storm Dorian, Typhoons Hagibis, and Faxai. The Cyber & Executive Risk and Specialty Lines divisions also saw releases, although these were somewhat offset by increased claims activity on liability books in recent years. The Political, Accident & Contingency division experienced a strengthening of $0.7 million. The 2018 year of account saw claims strengthening on the cyber and executive risk book due to increased claims activity and claims inflation, while the 2019 year of account was adversely affected by COVID-19 related claims.
raw_causal_phrases: Both the property and reinsurance divisions have benefitted from releases on some of the 2019 natural catastrophe events, namely Storm Dorian in the US and Typhoons Hagibis and Faxai in Japan.
Specialty Lines and cyber & executive risk had releases of $8.2m and $1.5m respectively.
Both specialty lines and cyber & executive risk have been impacted over the past few years by the increased claims seen on their liability books resulting in decreased releases.
Action taken in the marine division to remediate selected areas of the account... have resulted in a release of $1.9m in the division.

The 2018 year of account was closed with a loss on capacity of 2.7%... These increased claims have adversely affected the cyber and executive risk book and combined with some further deterioration on CyEx claims, have resulted in a claims strengthening on the 2018 year of account.

The 2019 year of account currently forecasts to close with a 2.5% loss on capacity having been adversely affected by claims experience related to the COVID-19 global pandemic, particularly in the contingency book.
